messages:
maya: Quick brain-dump — I'm iterating on the rollout metadata shape to add a couple of runtime hints: `traffic_hint` (float) and `stability_score` (0-1). Problem: older SDKs ignore new fields and keep hammering the same variant with naive retry/backoff logic. Thinking server-side compat shims + explicit client backpressure header. Sketch below.

maya: example payload I'm thinking about:
```json
{
  \"rollout\": {
    \"variant\": \"v2\",
    \"traffic_hint\": 0.65,
    \"stability_score\": 0.92,
    \"expires_at\": \"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z\"
  }
}
```

jon: curious — what do you mean by \"server-side compat shims\"? server mutating responses for old clients? :thinking_face:

maya: yeah — two levels: 1) a thin translation layer that maps new fields into legacy tokens the SDK understands (e.g., translate `traffic_hint` => `replicate_to_secondary=false`/`route_pct`), and 2) a soft-fallback policy where the server enforces rate-limits/backoff for clients that don't send the new `X-RW-Client-Compat` header.

sasha: +1 on header negotiation. Could we do `X-RW-Client-Compat: shim=v1` so we can iterate? servers can decide whether to honor hints vs. enforce defaults.

liam: slight worry: enforcing server-side backpressure per-client could be expensive to track at high QPS. Any heuristics to avoid state explosion?

maya: good call. Proposal: ephemeral token bucket keyed by `client_id` (already present for billing) kept in memcache with TTL = rollout `expires_at` + grace window (e.g., 1h). If missing, treat as legacy and apply conservative defaults.

erin: also consider a metric flag in the metadata for telemetry samplers. If we add `telemetry_tag: "shim-test-2026-06"`, we can sample 0.1% of legacy clients to surface misbehavior before forcing a rollout.

jon: can we avoid changing the wire format for now by using a top-level opaque `rollout_hint` blob? then shims can decode server-side but old clients still ignore it cleanly. less brittle for SDKs.

maya: that's an option. tradeoff: opaque blobs remove observability unless servers decode and emit canonical keys. i'm leaning to structured but optional fields + robust negotiation header.

dinesh: for telemetry add `compat_failure` counter with labels: `client_major`, `client_minor`, `route`, `variant`. capture `error_class` when stability drops. Sample aggressively for new variants.

liam: on backpressure algorithm: instead of strict per-client state we could do a hybrid — per-tenant token bucket + probabilistic client sampling for per-client enforcement. That keeps memory bounded.

maya: yep that matches my thinking. Implementation checklist: 
- [ ] define `X-RW-Client-Compat` header semantics (values: `none`, `shim=v1`, `features=rollout_hints`)
- [ ] rollout metadata schema: optional `traffic_hint`, `stability_score`, `telemetry_tag`, `compat_shim`
- [ ] server shim ruleset that maps hints -> legacy fields
- [ ] backpressure policy: tenant-bucket + sampled per-client enforcement
- [ ] telemetry: `compat_failure`, `shim_applied`, `legacy_penalty_throttle`

sasha: sounds good. small nit: include `min_supported_client` field so server can auto-enable stricter rules when most clients upgrade.

maya: yes, add `min_supported_client: \"2.4.0\"` — server can use semantic compare and only enable full hints when >= X% clients meet min.

erin: one more ops ask — make sure the shim emits a `X-RW-Shim-Applied: true` response header when it altered behavior so SDK logs can detect server-side intervention.

maya: agreed. i'll draft a short RFC with the schema and a toy implementation pseudocode for the shim and backpressure. will ping for review in this thread.

deploy-bot: deploy: rollout-hints-shim v0.1 deployed to staging by ci-pipeline at 2026-03-20T12:45:12Z :rocket:

jon: thanks — looking forward to the RFC, pls include failure modes and a rollback gate. :thumbsup:
